title: WPSS/1063/2017 of Hardik Kumar Gupta Vs Director General Medical, Health And Family Welfare AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No. 1063 of 2017
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Atul Bahuguana, Brief Holder for
the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Sagar Kothari, Advocate holding
brief of Mr. Ankur Sharma, Advocate for
the respondent no. 3.
Petitionerís father Late Jai Kumar
Gupta was a regular employee of State
Medical Department, serving on the post of
Chief Pharmacist in Government Joint
Hospital, Roorkee, who died on 24.11.2008
while still in service. It transpires that Jai
Kumar Gupta was earlier married to Smt.
Pushpa Gupta and one daughter, namely,
Ms. Anjali Gupta was born out of the said
wedlock. Jai Kumar Gupta obtained a
decree of divorce against his first wife and
married second time with Smt. Sureshna
Gupta on 21.09.1993 and petitioner
(Hardik Kumar Gupta) was born out of the
said wedlock on 11.07.1994.
Subsequently, on 09.02.1995, the divorce
decree, obtained by Jai Kumar Gupta, was
set aside on an application moved by his
first wife, consequently, his second
marriage became invalid,
Ultimately on 24.11.2008, Jai Kumar
Gupta died. Petitioner as well as Ms. Anjali
Gupta, daughter from the first wife, applied
for compassionate appointment. Claim of
Ms. Anjali Gupta was rejected by Director
General, Medical, Health & Family Welfare
vide order dated 22.02.2017, on the ground
that she is married and a married daughter
cannot be given appointment under Dying
in Harness Rules.

Petitioners claim was also rejected by
Director General, vide order dated
22.02.2017, in which he has relied upon
the opinion given by District Government
Counsel, Civil (in short ëDGCí), Haridwar,
which is impugned in the present writ
petition.
The opinion given by DGC (Civil),
Haridwar is on record as annexure No. 7 to
the writ petition, in which he has relied
upon the judgment rendered by Honíble
Madra High Court in the case of M.
Muthuraj Vs The Deputy General of
Police, Tamil Nadu, Police Department
Chennai reported in 2016 0 Supreme
(Mad) 3567 holding that a child born out of
void marriage cannot be considered for
compassionate appointment.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
and perused the record.
Honíble Madras High Court in the
case of M. Muthuraj (Supra) had
considered a Government order issued by
State of Tamil Nadu on 16.04.2002, in
which it is provided that children born out
of void marriages are not entitled to
compassionate appointment. Thus, it was
held that son of the deceased through his
second wife cannot be considered for
compassionate appointment. No such
Government Order, issued by Uttarakhand
Government, has been brought to the
notice of the Court, therefore, the aforesaid
judgment is distinguishable on facts.
Even otherwise also, at the time when
petitionerís father contracted second
marriage, his status was that of a divorcee
and also at the time when petitioner was
born. That status was subsequently altered
when the divorce decree obtained by his
father was set aside.

Moreover, in the present case, the
field is covered by Dying in Harness Rules,
1974, in which inclusive definition of
ëFamilyí has been given, which includes (i)
Wife or Husband; (ii) Sons; & (iii)
Unmarried and Widowed Daughters.
Thus, no distinction has been made
in the Rules applicable in the State of
Uttarakhand between children born out of
valid marriages and those born out of
invalid marriages.
A bare perusal of the impugned order
dated 22.02.2017 reveals that the Director
General, Medical, Health & Family Welfare,
Uttarakhand has rejected petitionerís claim
for compassionate appointment without
application of mind merely by relying upon
the opinion given by the DGC (Civil).
In such view of the matter, impugned
order dated 22.02.2017 cannot be
sustained.
Since the daughter born out of the
first marriage, namely, Ms. Anjali Gupta
has also claimed compassionate
appointment and a Full Bench of this Court
has held that married daughters are also
entitled to compassionate appointment,
therefore, it would be in the fitness of
things to direct the Director General, to
take decision afresh regarding the
competing claims made by the petitioner
and Ms. Anjali Gupta, in terms of Rule 7 of
the Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 which is
extracted below:-

ì7. Procedure when more than
one member of the family seeks
employment- If more than one
member of the family of the deceased
Government servant seeks
employment under these rules, the

Head of Office shall decide about the
suitability of the person for giving
employment. The decision will be
taken keeping in view also the overall
interest of the welfare of the entire
family, particularly the widow and the
minor members thereof.î
Accordingly, the impugned order
dated 22.02.2017 is quashed. Respondent
No. 1 is directed to re-consider the claim of
petitioner and respondent No. 4 ñ Ms.
Anjali Gupta for compassionate
appointment under Rule 7 of the Dying in
Harness Rules, 1974, within a period of ten
weeks from the date of production of
certified copy of this order.
With the aforesaid direction, writ
petition stands disposed of.
(Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
 02.04.2019
NEHA
